slides.heading: What it is
paras: Claude Code hooks are shell commands that run automatically at specific points in the Claude Code lifecycle — before a tool executes, after it executes, when a session starts…
slides.alt: DejaViewed carousel, slide 2 of 8. The idea. What it is. Claude Code hooks are shell commands that run automatically at specific points in the Claude Code lifecycle — before a tool executes, after it executes, when a session starts… From @jens.heitmann.

slides.heading: What a pro would do that you didn't ask for
paras: A platform engineer would treat hooks as production code that runs with your full user permissions on every tool call, so they would version the scripts in git, unit-test each one against recorded event payloads…

slides.heading: How you know it worked
items: bats or pytest suite: every hook passes allow, block, and malformed-stdin fixtures captured from the installed Claude Code version.
Headless claude -p --output-format stream-json transcripts showing the hook's block reason for a destructive command, with /tmp/hooktest-canary still present afterward.

slides.heading: Stop hook loops forever
paras: the session keeps restarting after every response and burns tokens.
exit 0 when stop_hook_active is true and cap retries.
